Section 01

The ground transportation industry

≈ 15 min
≡Definition

Ground transportation is pre-arranged, chauffeured car service: a customer books ahead, a licensed company sends a professional driver in a specific class of vehicle, and the price is agreed before the trip.

The company is called an operator. Limo Anywhere is the software an operator runs on. You will help operators use it.

»Example

"Pick me up at DFW at 11, take me to the Hilton, in an SUV." The operator quotes $165, sends Darrell in a Yukon, and bills the customer's company afterwards.

✓Key points
  • Not ride-hailing: no surge meter, price known up front
  • Booked in advance, often by an assistant for someone else
  • Who pays, who books and who rides can be three different people
  • Everything the software does hangs off one booked trip

What operators actually sell

Point-to-point

Address to address at a fixed price. The bread and butter of retail and corporate work.

Airport arrivals & departures

Pickups tied to a flight number; the driver's spot time moves with the flight. Customers are, in Brandon's words, "insane" about airport pickups.

Hourly / as-directed

The customer buys the vehicle and driver for a block of hours; drop-off is optional. Billed per hour with minimums.

Charter, tours & shuttles

Minibuses and motor coaches, often priced per passenger or per hour with tiered rates.

Who is in the picture

Every trip has more people attached than the one in the back seat. Understanding these roles is the single most useful thing you can do before opening a reservation screen, because Limo Anywhere's account model is built directly on them.

Billing contact

"Who pays?"

The person or department responsible for the bill. Might be an individual, or "Accounts Payable" at a corporation. Has the card on file or the invoice terms.

Booking contact

"Who called?"

The executive assistant or travel coordinator who makes the booking on someone else's behalf. Gets the confirmation.

Passenger

"Who rides?"

The person in the car. Gets the driver-on-the-way text. Often the same human as the other two in retail; often three different people in corporate work.

Operator

The transportation company running the software — your customer. Owns the fleet, the drivers, the rates and the client relationships.

Affiliate

Another operator, usually in a different city. Work sent to them is a farm-out; work received from them is a farm-in. Networks like LA Net, GNet, GroundSpan and Ground Exchange connect them.

Agent

A booking agent or travel partner paid a commission (say 5%) on every trip they send. Tracked so they can be paid at settlement.

Life of a trip

The same arc plays out thousands of times a day, and every status in Limo Anywhere maps to a point on it. Blue steps are done by office staff; green steps are done by the driver in the app.

How trips get priced

ModelHow it worksTypical use
Fixed (zone-to-zone)A pre-set price from zone A to zone B for a vehicle class. Zones are cities/zip groups or airports.Airport transfers, well-known routes
HourlyRate × hours, with a minimum number of hours per vehicle type. Below the minimum the vehicle is unavailable, not rounded up.As-directed, events, weddings
DistancePer-mile / per-km, usually tiered ("first mile $65, next 10 at $2, remaining at $1.50") so short trips still hit a minimum.Coverage outside your fixed-rate zones
Per passengerRate × number of passengers.Shuttles, coaches
Fixed-or-distanceLook for a fixed rate first; if no zone pair exists, fall back to distance.The most common airport setup

On top of the base come gratuity (20% is the industry norm), taxes, surcharges (fuel, STC), tolls/parking, wait time, extra stops and discounts. How those calculate against one another is a configuration decision — Section 06 covers it.

Vocabulary you will hear on every call

PU / DO
Pick-up and drop-off. "PU Date", "DO Time".
Spot time
When the driver should be in position, usually 15 min before PU.
Garage-out / Garage-in
Vehicle leaves and returns to base; used for hourly driver pay.
Farm-out / Farm-in
Sending a trip to, or receiving one from, an affiliate.
Meet & greet
Inside-terminal pickup with a name sign vs. curbside.
FBO
Fixed-base operator — a private-jet terminal. Its own routing type.
POI
Point of interest — a stored favourite place (stadium, hotel).
Direct bill
Corporate account invoiced on terms (e.g. net 30) instead of paying per trip.
Settle
Closing a done trip: confirm charges, driver/affiliate/agent pay, then file it.
ORES
Online Reservation System — the booking widget on the operator's website.
Knowledge check 01

Industry basics

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

A corporate executive assistant calls to book a car for her CEO; the company's accounts-payable department will be invoiced. Who is the passenger?

The assistant is the booking contact, AP is the billing contact, and the CEO — the person in the car — is the passenger.

A vehicle type has a 4-hour hourly minimum. A customer books it online for 2 hours. What happens?

Minimums are a gate on availability, not a rounding rule. The vehicle is filtered out, and depending on settings the customer sees "request a quote" or a hard stop.

You send a trip to a partner operator in Chicago because you have no cars there. That trip is a…

Work you send away is farmed out; the Chicago operator sees it as a farm-in.

"Fixed-or-distance" pricing means the system…

Fixed rates win when a zone pair exists; distance is the fallback for routes you haven't priced.
Section 02

Limo Anywhere at a glance

≈ 12 min
≡Definition

Limo Anywhere is a cloud-based back office for chauffeured transportation companies — reservations, dispatch, driver app, online booking, payments, invoicing, payroll and reports, all from one login.

»Example

A two-car operator in Dallas logs in at manage.mylimobiz.com, takes a phone booking, sends it to a driver's phone, charges the card and pays the driver — without leaving the browser.

✓Key points
  • Cloud-hosted since ~2010; about 5,700 operator companies use it
  • LA Net connects those operators to trade trips
  • Screens are simple; the settings are what make them behave
  • Nothing to install — a browser and a Company ID

The product family

Core

Back office (LA Core)

The browser app you will live in: manage.mylimobiz.com (or limoanywhere.com/login). Reservations, dispatch, accounts, settings, reports.

Customer-facing

ORES & Passenger Web App

The booking widget embedded on the operator's website, plus a mobile-first PWA. Customers self-book, request quotes and manage their account.

Driver-facing

Driver Anywhere

iOS/Android app where drivers accept offers, run status updates, track GPS, take pictures and even payments. Must be enabled per driver.

Ops

Limo Anywhere Mobile

Dispatcher's mobile app for managing the board on the go.

Network

LA Net & Partner Network

Farm trips in and out to other LA operators with real-time status sync; partner integrations with GroundSpan, GRiDD, Boston Coach and others.

Money

LAPA (LA Pay)

Integrated card processing. Tokenised cards, payment requests by email/SMS, batch payments at settlement. Stripe/Square outside the US.

Packages: Core, Plus and Black

LA Core

The base system

Everything in this module. Core also includes three free add-ons that an administrator activates from the add-on icons: Manifest Upload, Vehicle Maintenance Management and Incident Management.

LA Plus

Add-ons bundle

Premium tier layered on Core with extra automation. Upgraded from the add-ons dashboard ("Upgrade to Plus") by an administrator who signs the terms.

LA Black

Top tier

Adds features such as Auto Farm, GPS provider integration, surveys and driver/vehicle sync. Black operators show a badge in LA Net affiliate searches — a signal of higher automation.

1 · Company ID

Every operator has one (e.g. demo-limo-anywhere). Not case-sensitive. Never in the invite email — get it from your admin.

2 · Username

Set by the admin. Best practice: the user's email address, so there is nothing extra to remember.

3 · Password

PCI-DSS strength rules (12+ characters, mixed). Invite links expire within a day — use "Forgot password" if yours went stale. Click the eye icon to check what you typed.

4 · First-time prompts

Live-training banner, then "verify your profile" (mobile number), then a LAPA advert if the system isn't on it. Each shows once.

Drivers log in differently

Drivers use the same company ID but a username and password the operator types into the driver's profile (My Office › Company Resources › Drivers). Drivers cannot create their own accounts, and a new driver cannot log into Driver Anywhere until the "Driver Anywhere settings" tab is enabled for them.

Knowledge check 02

Product overview

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

A new driver was added yesterday but "could not log you in" appears in Driver Anywhere. Most likely cause?

Saving a driver does not enable the app. The operator must turn on the Driver Anywhere settings for that driver.

Which of these is the customer-facing booking widget?

ORES = Online Reservation System. LA Net is the affiliate network; LAPA is payments.

Where is a user's Company ID found?

For security the company ID is left out of the invite; the admin shares it.

Why does typing "DFW" in the airport field and tabbing away fail to price a trip?

The rate lookup matches on the stored code. Free text in the box is just text until you pick a result.

Finding your way

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

A trainee clicks the Reservations icon and then "New Reservations" expecting a blank form. What should they do instead?

"New Reservations" is a list of recently created trips. New Res (top bar) creates one.

Hourly rates for an SUV are set under which path?

Section 04

Taking and managing a reservation

≈ 45 min
≡Definition

A reservation is one booked trip: who is riding, when and where, in which vehicle, for how much, and who pays. It gets a confirmation number the moment it is created.

»Example

Conf# 15449 — Brandon Edley, Thu 11:00, DFW (AA 3211) → Savannah TX, SUV, $203.94, card on file, billed to Full Steam.

✓Key points
  • One trip = one reservation; a return is a second one
  • Three columns: Who · When & where · How & what
  • Only billing contact + PU date + PU time are needed to save
  • Work through the 14 short lessons in order

Three ways to reach the New Reservation screen

Click a route (or let it play) to watch the clicks. They all end on the same screen with a fresh confirmation number — pick the one that fits the call you're on.

4.1 Anatomy of the screen

Only three things are required to save

A billing contact, a PU date and a PU time. Everything else can come later. (Some companies add "payment method" as a fourth requirement in preferences.) Every click of New Res generates the next sequential confirmation number immediately — the yellow banner reminds you it exists but is not saved. Close without saving and it lands in Reservations › Unfinalized.

Required by the system

To press Save

  1. Billing contact
  2. PU date
  3. PU time
  4. (Payment method, if your company switched on that requirement)
Required by a good booking

Before you hang up

  1. Passenger name and mobile number (texts go there)
  2. Pick-up and drop-off stored in routing — with flight number for airports
  3. Service type and vehicle type
  4. A rate applied and read back to the caller
  5. Payment method (card on file, new card, or direct bill for accounts)
  6. Passenger count, luggage, child seats, special notes

Save

Top or bottom, same button. Warns about driver/car conflicts but never hard-blocks.

Payments

Record a payment, use a card on file, or send a LAPA payment / card-on-file request link.

Copy · Round Trip

Duplicate once or on a schedule; or create the mirrored return trip.

Email / Fax · Print

Confirmations, trip sheets, custom forms, invoices — to the contacts on the account.

Res log

Field-by-field change history with user, old and new value; add comments; export.

Link

Group reservations and replicate changes across them. Red = links exist.

More ▾

Incident log, Settle, Quote log, Dispatch log, Delete, Unfinalize.

Affiliate: LA Net / Manually

Farm-out buttons in the right column, visible when trip type is Farm-out.

Lesson 3 of 19

4.3 The "who" column and the account model

≡Definition

An account is a person, not a company. It can play three roles — billing contact (pays), booking contact (calls), passenger (rides). People at one company are linked only by an identical Company Name.

»Example

Jonathan (billing + booking + passenger, company "Corn") and Brian (passenger only, company "Corn"). Brian's trips can bill to Jonathan because the company names match exactly.

✓Key points
  • Account #, Billing Contact and Company Name are one search box with three labels
  • Typing 3 letters shows matches — click one to attach the account
  • Typing a name and tabbing away stores text only: no history, no cards, no rates
  • Attached correctly, the passenger icon lists that account's riders

What attaching an account brings in

Cards on file (from billing contact and passenger), account-specific rates in the ACCT tab, default payment method and terms, stored addresses, account notes, and the trip in the account's history.

Ad-hoc callers

Someone with no account can still be typed in as billing contact and passenger. Fine for one-offs; use Create New Acct if they will book again.

Why duplicates hurt

A second account for the same person splits their history, cards and rates in two, and someone has to merge them later by hand. Search first, create last.

Rule of thumb

Search, then select. If you clear the account with the CL button, both the account number and the billing contact go — they cannot exist without each other. Enter the passenger's mobile number: automated "driver on the way" texts go to that field.

Lesson 4 of 19

4.4 Routing: pickups, stops, waits and drop-offs

≡Definition

Routing is the list of places on a trip. Each place has a type (Address, Airport, Seaport, FBO, POI) and an action (Pick-up, Drop-off, Stop, Wait).

»Example

Airport tab → DFW, AA 3211 → click Pick-up. Address tab → 1104 Cotton Exchange Dr → click Drop-off. Both now sit in Stored Routing Information.

✓Key points
  • Pick the tab, enter the place, then click the action
  • The action is what stores it — clicking Pick-up on an empty form errors
  • Select Google's standardised address; typed-as-is addresses get no mileage
  • One trip = one pick-up, optional stops/waits, one drop-off

Stored Routing Information
No routing info stored

Address

Type street and city; Google verifies it and adds zip and country. Pick the standardised match — "use as originally entered" gets no mileage.

Airport

Stored Airports are your favourites (enabled under Company Resources). Add airline + flight number: arrivals sync the spot time to the flight; departures are informational.

POI · FBO · Seaport

Stored venues, private-jet terminals and cruise ports with their own lists. Many agents type a venue name in the Address tab instead and let Google find it.

Stop vs Wait

Both are places between pick-up and drop-off. A Wait carries a time so wait-time charges can apply.

One trip = one route

Several passengers on different flights cannot be tracked on one reservation — make one per flight and give them the same driver. Multi-leg days are separate reservations (lesson 4.12).

Time In ≠ pick-up time

The Time In field on a routing item is a note, not the pickup. The times that matter are PU date/time, DO time and spot time at the top.

≡Definition

  • You can also type straight into the line items

Hourly trips

Duration defaults to 1 hour. Updating the DO time updates duration, but not the other way round. With the "auto-populate number of hours" preference on, the duration flows into the Per Hour multiplier; otherwise type it. Rate lookups with the wrong duration produce nonsense like 0.03 × $350.

4.6 Payment info: how the trip gets paid

≡Definition

The Payment Info tab records how this trip will be paid. It never takes money — charging happens through the Payments action in the toolbar.

»Example

Priya’s account is Direct Bill/Invoice, so Payment Method defaults to that and no card is needed. A walk-in caller instead needs a card entered or requested before Save will go through.

✓Key points
  • Defaults come from the account’s Financial Data tab
  • Direct Bill/Invoice is only offered when a real account is attached
  • Cards are tokenised — you see only the last four digits
  • Company Preferences can make a card required to save

Payment Info tab

Beside "Bill To & Pax". Payment method (defaults from the account), cards from the billing contact's or passenger's account, a new card, PO / voucher numbers. Direct Bill/Invoice is only available when a real account is attached. Taking or requesting a payment happens via the Payments action.

Taking the money

Nothing is charged from this tab. Payments in the toolbar charges a card or records cash/cheque; Send payment request emails the customer a secure page where they type their own card — the safest way to take a card over the phone. Deposits and part-payments show up as Payments/Deposits against the Grand Total.

Lesson 7 of 19

4.7 Notes: four kinds, and who reads them

≡Definition

A note is free text attached to a trip. Which box you type it in decides who sees it — and one of those audiences is the customer.

»Example

“Meet at door D22” belongs in trip notes (the customer reads it). “VIP, do not chat” belongs in driver notes (internal). Both on the same trip.

✓Key points
  • Trip notes print on confirmations — the customer sees them
  • Driver / dispatch notes are internal
  • Bill To & Pax notes come from the account and repeat on every trip
  • A routing note belongs to one stop and prints on the trip sheet

Tour · The four places a note can live

Where each one ends up

Three kinds of notes

Trip notes print on confirmations; Bill To & Pax notes pull from the account; driver / dispatch notes are internal. Routing notes belong to a stop. Read the labels — customers see some of these.

Read the label before you type

The single most common note mistake is putting an internal comment where the customer will read it. If you are not sure which box you are in, look at the label above it — and when in doubt, put it in driver / dispatch notes, which nobody outside the company ever sees.

Lesson 8 of 19

4.8 Extras: passengers, signs, seats and labels

≡Definition

The extras are the small fields that decide whether the trip actually goes right on the day — and the ones you can report on afterwards.

»Example

Three passengers, five bags, an infant seat and a booster, a greeting sign reading NAIR / FULL STEAM, group name “FullSteam Q3 offsite”.

✓Key points
  • Only the primary passenger gets automated messages
  • Pax and luggage counts are checked against vehicle capacity
  • Child-seat count multiplies the child-seat line item
  • Occasion, Source, Group and Arranged-by are reporting fields

Additional passengers

Add names and emails for the manifest. Only the primary passenger receives automated messages, but many corporate clients require every rider recorded.

Greeting sign, child seats, luggage

Greeting sign text for meet-and-greet; child seat required + count (multiplies the child-seat line item); passenger and luggage counts checked against vehicle capacity.

Occasion · Source · Group · Arranged by

Free-text lists you can report on later: what the trip was for, how the customer found you, a group name that ties 10 wedding cars together. Managed under My Office › List Management.

Read-back script

A pop-up on first (or every) save that reads the booking back to the caller — passenger, date, time, PU/DO, fare, payment method — in bold from live data. Templates per service type under My Office › Company Settings › Read Back Script; turned on in Company Preferences › Reservations.

Lesson 9 of 19

4.9 Putting a driver and a car on the trip

≡Definition

Choosing a driver and a car on the reservation is a plan. It writes two names on the trip. It sends nothing, tells nobody, and the trip stays Unassigned on the board.

»Example

Pick Darrell in the Driver list and Sedan3 in the Car list, press Save — Darrell’s phone stays silent. Only a status change dispatches him (next lesson).

✓Key points
  • Driver, Preferred Driver and Car are three different fields
  • A car that does not match the vehicle type warns, it does not block
  • Primary and Secondary tabs let two cars run one trip
  • Assigning here is optional — dispatch can do it later on the board

Tour · Putting a driver and a car on the trip

Sedan (SED)
— none —▾

⚠ Warning, not a block
Dispatch board
UNUnassigned · no driver on this trip

Driver vs Preferred Driver

Driver is who is actually doing this trip. Preferred Driver is a note of who the customer likes — it is used when dispatch is deciding, and it can be defaulted from the account so it appears on every booking.

Car ≠ vehicle type

Vehicle type is what was sold (Sedan, SUV). The car is a specific vehicle in the fleet. Picking a car outside the sold type raises a warning so you can catch “we sold an SUV and put a sedan on it” before the passenger does.

Two cars, one trip

Eight passengers and one sedan? Either book two reservations, or use the Secondary tab to add a second driver and car to this trip. Secondary has its own rate section so the extra car can be priced.

The trap

New agents put a driver on and tell the customer “you’re all set, Darrell will be there”. Darrell knows nothing about it. Until the status changes, nothing has left the office.

Lesson 10 of 19

4.10 Dispatching: offering vs assigning a driver

≡Definition

A status is where a trip is in its life (Unassigned → Offered → Assigned → On the way … Done). Your company names them; each is mapped to one of Limo Anywhere's built-in states, and that mapping drives what happens.

»Example

Pick Darrell in the dropdown: nothing happens. Change status to Dispatched (mapped to "Offered to driver"): his phone buzzes with Accept / Reject. He accepts → status flips to Assigned by itself.

✓Key points
  • A driver name on the trip is a plan, not a dispatch
  • Offered = driver may accept or reject (contractors)
  • Assigned = no choice, straight to Upcoming (employees)
  • Mapping lives in System Settings › System Mapping; each status has a code, name and colour

Don't touch these

"Online and eFarm-in", "Dispatched" and "Cancelled by Affiliate" have special functions. Deactivate other statuses by dragging to Inactive or clicking ×.

Status-to-time mapping

Stamp times automatically: e.g. On the Way → Garage-out, Arrived → Spot time, Dropped off → DO time. Choose whether to overwrite times already saved.

Drivers can't go backwards

Driver Anywhere only offers the driver-flow statuses, in order; Circling is the one optional step. The office can set any status from the reservation or the dispatch grid.

Lesson 11 of 19

4.11 Copy and recurring trips

≡Definition

Copy makes a new reservation from an existing one — same passenger, routing and rates, a new date and a new confirmation number. It can also generate a whole recurring series in one press.

»Example

A school run every weekday until 20 December: open the trip, Copy, frequency Every workday, End by 20 Dec, email confirmations off, Copy Reservation.

✓Key points
  • Every copy gets its own confirmation number
  • Frequency + end condition build a recurring series
  • Turn confirmations off when generating many
  • What carries over is set in Company Preferences › Reservations

Copy

From the open reservation click Copy. Change any field (date, vehicle, service, driver), tick or untick Send email confirmations, Link copy to original and Copy affiliate rate data, then Copy Reservation. For a recurring trip set the next date, a frequency (daily / every N days / workdays / weekly…), and an end — after N occurrences or on a date. Leave confirmations off when generating dozens. What is carried over is governed by Company Preferences › Reservations.

“Same as last time”

The everyday case: find last week’s trip (Dispatch › right-click › Copy, or open it and press Copy), change the date, End After 1 occurrence, done. Check the driver and car — a copy keeps them, which is right for next Tuesday and wrong for next March.

Tour · The Copy dialog

Continuation trips: one passenger, several legs in a day

EXAMPLEThe itinerary09:00 DFW → hotel · 13:00 hotel → client office · 19:00 office → restaurant → hotel
RULEOne leg = one reservationEach leg with its own start time is a separate reservation, never extra stops on the first one. Stops are for pauses within a leg (the restaurant).
HOWCopy the first legSave leg 1, press Copy, change time and routing, keep the same driver and car, tick Link copy to original. Repeat for leg 3.
WHYSeparate legs give you…a status per leg on Dispatch, correct pricing per leg, flight tracking on the airport leg, and Replicate Changes across the linked set if the passenger's details change.
Or make it hourly

If the client wants the car all day at their disposal, book one hourly / as-directed reservation for the block instead of separate legs — the rate is per hour and the drop-off is optional.

Lesson 12 of 19

4.12 Round trips and continuation trips

≡Definition

A round trip is the return leg, created from a saved outbound trip with the pick-up and drop-off already swapped. It is a second reservation, not a second half of the first one.

»Example

Home → DFW on 16 Sep (Conf# 15501). Round Trip → DFW → Home on 19 Sep with flight AA 1180 (Conf# 15502), linked to the first.

✓Key points
  • Save the outbound first — Round Trip needs a saved trip
  • You must ask for the return date and time
  • An airport return needs its own airline and flight number
  • Two confirmation numbers, each with its own rate, driver and status

Round trip — step by step

  1. Book and save the outbound trip first (e.g. home → DFW, 11:00).
  2. Click Round Trip in the toolbar.
  3. Ask the caller: "What date and time do you want to come back?" Enter the return PU date/time; for an airport return add the inbound flight.
  4. PU and DO are already swapped. Tick Link to original so both trips reference each other on paperwork.
  5. Email confirmations now or later. Press Create. You now have two confirmation numbers; the return has its own rate, driver and status.

Why not one long trip?

Because a trip has one pick-up time, one driver, one status and one price. A return three days later shares none of those. Two reservations let dispatch run them independently and let the customer be charged correctly for each.

4.13 Linking trips and Replicate Changes

≡Definition

A link is an operational relationship between reservations. Once trips are linked, Replicate Changes can push a correction from one of them onto all the others in a single press.

»Example

Ten trips were booked without the account attached. Fix one, link the other nine to it, tick “bill-to / passenger”, Replicate Information — all ten now bill correctly.

✓Key points
  • Links are always to the reservation you started from
  • The Linked Reservations tab unlinks; Link Reservations searches for trips to add
  • You choose exactly which data points get pushed
  • There is no undo

Tour · Link and Replicate Changes

Billing contact Priya Nair · Full Steam pushed to every linked trip.There is no undo.

Linking groups reservations so you can see them together and update them in one go. Click Link (red when links already exist). The Linked Reservations tab lists the group — tick and Remove Link Between Selected to unlink. The Link Reservations tab lists every unsettled trip in the system; search by field and date range, tick, then Link Selected. Links are always to the reservation you started from, so link each new trip from that same one.

Replicate Changes is the payoff. Edit one reservation, click Link › Replicate Changes, choose all linked or only selected, tick the data points to push — bill-to / booked-by / passenger, pickup date and times, routing, pax and luggage counts, notes, rates, service and vehicle type, driver and car, contact info, seats, referral source, payment method, rental agreement — and press Replicate Information. Typical use: ten trips booked without the account attached; fix one, link the rest, replicate the billing contact. There is no undo.

Group name vs. link

A group name (right column) is a label for reporting — "Smith wedding" pulls all ten cars into one report. A link is an operational relationship that lets you replicate changes. Linking also prints a "linked to #…" note on paperwork; it changes no pricing or dispatch logic.

Lesson 14 of 19

4.14 Quotes: leads that are not yet reservations

≡Definition

A quote is a price request that is not yet a booking — no card, no promise. It lives under the Quotes icon, not on the dispatch board, until it is converted.

»Example

A visitor on the website asks "how much from DFW to Lewisville?" It arrives as quote #15495. You price it, email it; she clicks the link, enters a card, and it becomes reservation #15496.

✓Key points
  • Created from the website, the New Res ▾ arrow, or Rate › Quote
  • Status is locked to Quote
  • Email a Response Template — the convert link is what lets the customer accept
  • Conversion cannot be undone
1Open the requestQuotes › Action › Open Quote Request. Details left, rate toolbar right with counts of matching rates.
2Price itClick a found rate (Fixed, Hourly, Pax, Account, Promo, Misc, Distance) or type into the rate table. Save.
3Email quoteLoad a Response Template, check the merged text, Send and Log Response. Logged in Response/Change Log.
4Customer convertsThey click #CONVERT_LINK#, enter a card, and the quote becomes a live reservation on its own.
5…or you convertConvert icon on the quote toolbar. Then payment is on you to collect. Conversion cannot be reversed.
Which conversion path?

Customer clicks the link when you emailed the quote — they enter their card, the system converts it, you touch nothing. You press Convert when the customer is on the phone saying "book it" — then take the card or payment method yourself right away. Either way the quote number disappears from Quotes and a reservation appears with a Quote log entry.

Response templates

Quotes › Response Templates. Title + text with tags in # marks: #CUST_NAME#, #COMPANY#, #QUOTE_SUMMARY#, #PRICE_QUOTE#, #PHONE#, #EMAIL#, #WEB_ADDRESS#, #RATE_DISCLAIMER# and the essential #CONVERT_LINK# / #CONVERT_URL#. HTML is allowed. An initial response template goes out automatically the moment a web quote arrives.

Quote toolbar

Save · History (response log) · Email · Convert · Exit without saving · Delete. New quote notifications are configured under Quotes › Quote Settings (email / SMS to a named user) — they do not raise the dispatch flag the way online bookings do.

Lesson 15 of 19

4.15 Online bookings and farm-ins: Accept / Reject

≡Definition

Trips that arrive from outside — website bookings, LA Net farm-ins, partner-network trips — wait in Reservations › Online & eFarm-in until someone accepts or rejects them.

»Example

ABC Limo in Chicago farms you a trip for their client landing at DFW tomorrow. It shows with status "Booked / unaccepted"; you check it and press Accept; it moves to Unassigned on Dispatch and ABC becomes the billing contact.

✓Key points
  • Not on the board until accepted (unless auto-accept is on)
  • Rates are editable before accepting
  • You choose which emails go out
  • Reject with a reason if something can't be fixed by phone
1Open the tabReservations › Online & eFarm-in. A flag on the toolbar tells you something is waiting.
2Accept / RejectLink on the left of the row opens the review pop-up.
3Check the ratesEdit the rate table if needed and press Update Rate Information.
4Choose emailsAccepted/rejected notice, standard confirmation/cancellation, both, or neither. Message text is editable per trip.
5SubmitSubmit and Close or Submit and Go to Reservation. Accepted → Unassigned on the board.

What to check before you press Accept

  1. Date, time and time zone — a farm-in from another city arrives in the sender's time; confirm it matches your dispatch time.
  2. Routing complete — real pick-up and drop-off, airport code + airline + flight number on airport legs, terminal / meet-and-greet notes.
  3. Vehicle type you actually have — and free at that time; check Dispatch for conflicts.
  4. The rate — what the affiliate is paying you (their farm-out cost) vs. your own price for the same trip; edit the rate table if it's below your minimum, or reject.
  1. Who pays — for LA Net farm-ins the sending company is the billing contact with Direct Bill; for web bookings a card or accepted payment method.
  2. Passenger contact — mobile number present so driver-on-the-way texts work (some senders redact it; then all contact goes through the affiliate).
  3. Special requests — child seats, luggage, accessibility, VIP.
  4. Then tick which emails go out and Submit. Reject with a reason if any item fails and can't be fixed by phone.

The four email choices — pick one deliberately

Both

Accept/reject notice and the standard confirmation (or cancellation). The normal choice for a clean web booking you are happy with.

Notice only

Tells the sender you took it, without sending the customer a confirmation yet — useful on a farm-in where the affiliate, not the passenger, owns the customer relationship.

Confirmation only

The customer gets their confirmation; no accept/reject notice goes back. Rare, but used when the sender does not want the extra mail.

Neither

The KB’s own tip: send nothing while you review the trip or phone the customer, then email from the reservation once everything is right.

The message is per trip

The accept/reject notification text can be edited inside this window before you submit — so you can write “accepted, but please confirm the flight number” instead of the standard wording.

Tour · The Accept / Reject window

Lesson 16 of 19

4.16 Farm-out: sending a trip to an affiliate

≡Definition

A farm-out is a trip you sell to your customer but hand to another operator (an affiliate) to drive. You pay the affiliate less than the customer pays you.

»Example

Your Dallas client needs a car in New York. You quote $220, farm it to an LA Net affiliate in NYC for $170, and watch their driver's statuses on your own board.

✓Key points
  • The affiliate must exist under Company Resources › Affiliates
  • LA Net affiliates: statuses sync both ways in real time
  • Others: trip sheet by email, statuses by phone
  • Set trip type Farm-out → affiliate → farm-out cost → Save → LA Net

When do we farm out?

Typical reasons
  1. Out of area — the pick-up is in a city where the company has no cars (the most common case).
  2. No vehicle of that type — the customer wants a coach or a stretch and the fleet has none.
  3. Fleet fully booked — a busy day, every car and driver already assigned at that time.
  4. Not worth running — a short trip far from base, or a one-way that would leave a car stranded.
  5. Keeping the customer — a corporate account travels nationwide; you farm out rather than say no and lose the account.
How the decision is made
  1. Quote the customer your price first — they never see the affiliate's price.
  2. Find an affiliate in that city (LA Net search, or a known partner); prefer LA Net / LA Black partners for real-time status updates and easier billing.
  3. Agree the farm-out cost — what you pay them — leaving a margin (companies typically aim for 10–25% below the customer price).
  4. Confirm the affiliate has the vehicle type and is happy with flight tracking / meet-and-greet needs.
  5. Send it (below), then watch for the Affiliate Reference # and the accepted status. Chase if it stays "Offered to affiliate".

How to send it

LA Net affiliate

Six steps, in this order

  1. Set trip type to Farm-out (right column).
  2. Pick the affiliate.
  3. Open the Farm-Out Costs tab in the rates section and enter what you will pay them — the Affiliate Total is all they see; your Grand Total stays private.
  4. Save. The LA Net button errors if you skip this.
  5. Click LA Net, match their vehicle type, tick Transfer affiliate rate, Complete.
  6. Check the Affiliate Reference # field: their confirmation number means it arrived. Status becomes Offered to Affiliate, then your "Affiliate Is Assigned" status once they accept.
Outside Limo Anywhere

Manual farm-out

Prerequisites: an account for them (Accounts, type Billing Contact + Affiliate, payment method Direct Bill/Invoice — for the farm-in direction) and an affiliate profile with email and "Send trip ticket by: Email".

  1. On the trip: status Farm-out Unassigned, type Farm-out, affiliate name, farm-out cost. Save.
  2. Email/Fax › Affiliate Trip Sheet to their address.
  3. They confirm by reply or phone; you update statuses yourself.

Real-time updates

Network › My Company Profile › Receive real-time updates: Yes — on both companies. Then their driver's On the way / Arrived / Dropped off update your board one-to-one via the affiliate statuses.

Choosing an affiliate

Core has no automatic routing. The affiliate search box also matches city and other profile columns; assignment priority only orders the list. Auto Farm (LA Black add-on) offers trips by region to assigned affiliates via email/SMS and escalates when nobody accepts.

Paying them

At settlement the farm-out cost flows to Payables › Pay Affiliate. Farm-ins bill the sending operator through their account (invoice or payment request).

A trip that came in as a farm-in normally cannot be farmed out again. To allow it, go Network › Partner Network › Partners, open the partner and tick “Designate trips from partner as In-House”. The two directions, side by side

Lesson 17 of 19

4.17 After it's booked: changes and settled trips

In plain words — Customers change their minds: a new flight, a different hotel, one more passenger. Changing a saved reservation is normal and easy. The one state you must respect is settled — that means the trip has been closed and the money and pay recorded, so changing it is a deliberate, logged action.

Making a change to a live reservation

1Find itType the confirmation number in Find (top bar), or right-click the row on Dispatch › Detailed Edit, or search Reservations / the account's History.
2Edit and SaveChange the field — time, routing, vehicle, passenger, rate. Re-apply the rate table if the change affects price. Save.
3Tell the people affectedCustomer: Email/Fax › confirmation again (it isn't automatic). Driver: if already assigned, they see the updated details in the app; change the driver or status if the plan changed. Affiliate: LA Net farm-outs sync; manual ones need an email.
4Check the trailThe Res log records who changed what, old and new value. Use it when "someone changed my booking".

Changing many at once

Same passenger, five trips this week, new phone number? Link them and use Replicate Changes (lesson 4.13). For a whole account, edit the account and the next bookings pick it up.

Cancelling

Change the status to your Cancelled (or Late cancelled / No show) status — never delete. Cancelled trips keep their history, can carry a cancellation fee, and still need settling. Send the cancellation email from Email/Fax.

Deleting

More › Delete is for true mistakes (a test booking, a duplicate). It asks for the master delete password and the trip moves to Reservations › Deleted.

What "settled" means

DONETrip finishedStatus mapped to Completed (or cancelled). It now appears under the Settle icon.
PAIDBalance is zeroPayment taken, or the account is Direct Bill / Invoice. Charges corrected (wait time, tolls, extra stop).
PAYDriver / affiliate / agent pay confirmedWhat each party earns on this trip is recorded on the settle window.
SETTLEDFiledPress Settle. The trip is locked: it feeds driver payroll, affiliate payables and invoices. On Dispatch it shows your settled status.
Changing a settled trip

Reopen, fix, re-settle

  1. Settle icon › Settled Reservations tab (or Find the confirmation number).
  2. Click Details on the row to open the settle window.
  3. Press REOPEN. The trip is unsettled and editable again.
  4. Make the change — a missed toll, wrong gratuity, wrong driver pay. If the balance changes, take or refund the difference.
  5. Press UPDATE to save, or SETTLE to file it again.
Before you reopen

Think about what already left

If a driver payroll log, an affiliate pay entry or an invoice has already been generated from this trip, your change will not flow into it automatically — tell accounting so they can regenerate or adjust. Reopening is meant for corrections ("settled in error"), not routine edits. Every reopen is logged.

Lesson 18 of 19

4.18 Incidents, done and the close-out

Incident log

More › Incident: log a late pickup, damage, lost item or accident with free text; tick Incident Resolved when handled. Show the Incident Report column in Dispatch › Grid Setup — a red flag appears on flagged trips; edit via right-click › Detailed Edit.

Done means the status says so

Time passing completes nothing. A trip is complete when its status is mapped to Completing/Completed (or a cancelled state). Then it appears in Settle, which is where charges, driver / affiliate / agent pay are confirmed and the trip is filed.

"I can't settle it"

Four causes: status not mapped to a completing/cancelled state; already settled (see lesson 4.17); Direct Bill/Invoice needed but not set; or an unpaid balance — take the payment (PMTS) or correct the rate data. Import Reservations (Excel template, 5 pm–5 am CT only) exists for large group bookings but is legacy — use with care.

Lesson 19 of 19

4.19 Knowledge check

Knowledge check 04

Reservation process

Pass mark: 6 of 9.

You typed "Brandon Edley" in Billing Contact and tabbed to the next field without clicking a search result. Later you look at Brandon's account history. The trip is…

The billing-contact field is a search. Selecting a result attaches the account; typing does not.

A caller wants an SUV from DFW to downtown. You entered the airport but the "Pick-up" button gives an error. Why?

Enter the location, then click Pick-up / Drop-off / Stop / Wait to store it.

You selected a driver and car on the reservation and saved. What does the driver see in Driver Anywhere?

Naming a driver only records it. The status change is the dispatch action.

A web customer requested a quote. What converts it into a reservation without you taking payment by phone?

The convert link in the emailed quote takes the customer to a payment page; the quote converts itself.

You set a trip to Farm-out, chose the affiliate and clicked LA Net, but got "please set the trip to farm out". What did you skip?

The farm-out type and affiliate must be saved on the record before the LA Net action can read them.

Ten reservations for one client were entered without the account attached. Fastest fix?

Link groups them; Replicate pushes the corrected billing contact to all linked trips. Group name is only a report label.

An affiliate accepted your LA Net farm-out but their driver's "On the way" never shows on your board. Most likely?

Real-time LA Net updates require the setting to be Yes on both sides.

A client needs 09:00 airport → hotel, 13:00 hotel → office and 19:00 office → hotel, same day. How do you book it?

Each leg with its own start time is its own reservation; stops are only for pauses within one leg. Linking keeps them together.

A trip was settled yesterday and the driver now reports a $12 toll that was never added. What do you do?

Settled trips are locked. Reopen is the deliberate, logged way to correct one.
Section 05

Dispatch: running the day

≈ 25 min
≡Definition

Dispatch is the screen for today: every trip for the date in one table, with the driver, the car and the live status. Reservations is the order book; Dispatch is the kitchen.

»Example

09:40 — a dispatcher sees Brandon's 11:00 airport pickup still Unassigned, puts Darrell and SUV-3 on it, sets status to Dispatched, and watches it turn Assigned when Darrell accepts on his phone.

✓Key points
  • One row per trip; colour = status
  • Right-click a row for every action
  • Change status here to offer or assign drivers
  • Grid Setup lets each dispatcher shape the board

The row shows the essentials — confirmation number, pickup time, status, passenger, pickup and drop-off, vehicle type, driver and car — and its colour tells you the status at a glance (your company picks the colours).

Lesson 2 of 6

5.2 Assigning and dispatching a driver

Two separate things happen, and new agents mix them up. Putting a name on the trip — choosing a driver and a car in the row — is just the office's plan. Dispatching — changing the status — is what actually sends the job to the driver's phone. Nothing reaches the driver until the status changes.

1Pick driver + carChoose from the dropdowns in the row. The car must belong to the requested vehicle type, or you get a warning (not a block).
2AStatus → OfferedYour "Dispatched" status. Driver gets a push notification with Accept / Reject. Accept → status flips to Assigned by itself. Reject → back to Unassigned, driver cleared.
2BStatus → AssignedNo choice for the driver — the trip simply appears in their Upcoming list. Usual for employees; Offered is usual for contractors.
3Driver runs the flowOn the way → (Circling) → Arrived → Customer in car → Dropped off → Done. Each tap updates your board within seconds.
4Watch the exceptionsA trip stuck in Offered too long, a rejection, a flight delay, a conflict warning — those are the dispatcher's real job.

Statuses are your words, mapped to LA's

Your company may call it "Dispatched", "Code 10" or "Sent". What matters is which canonical state it is mapped to in System Settings › System Mapping. That mapping is what triggers the driver notification.

Conflicts

If Grid Setup › Conflicts is on, the board warns when the same driver or car is on two overlapping trips. It warns; it does not stop you.

Farm-outs on the board

A farmed-out trip shows the affiliate's statuses (Offered to affiliate → Affiliate assigned → Affiliate driver on the way…) when real-time updates are on for both companies.

5.4 Set up your grid

Every dispatcher can shape the board to their own eyes. Click Grid Setup on the Dispatch page. Five tabs; press Update Dispatch Grid Fields to save any of them.

Grid Setup — columns

Tick the columns you want, drag them up (left) or down (right), set widths in pixels. Tip: turn on Special System Notification Flags to get the ❗ column.

Date / Time

Date and time formats, the business hours the grid shows, and Refresh Dispatch Every — choose Auto Updates so changed trips glow on screen without you pressing refresh (must be enabled in company settings first).

Conflicts

On or off: warn when a driver or car is double-booked.

My Prefs — just for you

Hide statuses you don't need (e.g. Done), colour airport runs or VIPs, show contact info on hover, choose your map provider, font size, row height, and whether the whole row or only the status cell is coloured.

Company Prefs — for everyone

Which flags appear: unpaid balance, child seat, last-minute booking (you choose the window), driver rejected, Driver Anywhere messaging.

Filters & presets (new grid)

Column + Operator + Value, e.g. Driver · Equals · Darrell, or Conf# · Contains · 154. Save as a preset or a permanent tab such as "Airport runs today".

5.5 Map, GPS and calendar

Map view & directions

The new grid's Map view plots today's pickups. On any grid, right-click a trip › Map to get directions from your chosen provider (Google Maps, MapQuest…) — set per user under My Prefs.

GPS tab

Driver's side of the same picture

In Driver Anywhere the driver taps On duty, picks their car, sees Upcoming / In progress / Pending, and moves through the statuses in order (they can skip Circling but never go backwards). 5.6 Knowledge check

Knowledge check 05

Dispatch

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

You chose Darrell and car SUV-3 on a row and saved. Darrell says he never got the trip. Why?

Names on the row are the plan; the status change is the dispatch.

A trip has been in "Dispatched" (Offered) for 40 minutes. What does that tell you?

Offered means waiting for the driver's Accept. That visibility is the point of the status.

Where do you make the board colour VIP passengers, only for your own login?

My Prefs is per user; Company Prefs is for everyone.

A customer calls: "Where is my car?" Fastest way to see the driver's live position?

Section 06

Basic configuration: the switches behind the screens

≈ 35 min
≡Definition

Configuration is the set of switches that decide how the software behaves for this company: what it sells, what it drives, how it prices, who may log in.

»Example

"Why doesn't the SUV show up for airport trips?" → the SUV vehicle type isn't ticked for the From Airport service type. Five clicks in Company Resources fixes it.

✓Key points
  • Section 03 = where things are; this section = what to set
  • Rarely changed, constantly felt
  • Each lesson is one small task
  • Rates are the part people find hardest — go slowly there
6.1 Company settings6.2 System users6.3 Service types6.4 Vehicles & fleet6.5 Rate basics6.6 Fixed rates & zones6.7 Hourly, pax, distance6.8 Promos & fees6.9 Reservation prefs6.10 Knowledge check
Lesson 1 of 10

6.1 Company settings and preferences

In plain words — "Configuration" means the switches that decide how the software behaves for this company. Most were set when the company joined. As an agent you will rarely flip them, but you will be asked "why does it do that?" every day, and the answer is almost always one of these switches. This section teaches the ones you can safely touch and where the rest live.

Start at My Office›Company Settings. Two pages matter most:

Contact Information

Company name, address, phone and the email addresses used on outgoing paperwork. Upload a logo and it replaces the text block on confirmations — so put the phone and email on the logo itself. Never use a free Gmail/Yahoo address here: emails go out through Limo Anywhere's mail service and need the company's own domain to be trusted.

Company Preferences

Seven tabs of switches. Press Update My Company Preferences at the bottom or the change is lost. The tabs are summarised below; the Reservations tab gets its own lesson (6.9).

TabWhat lives there (the ones you'll notice)
GeneralTime zone · date & time format · currency · default state · address format · which page opens at login · default trip type (In-house / Farm-in / Farm-out) · alert for new online reservations · Master delete password · custom labels (call a passenger a "guest", a reservation a "job")
Forms & ReportsWhat customers, drivers and affiliates see on paperwork: show rates to drivers or not, itemised charges on confirmations, drop-off time on emails, signature line on trip sheets, font sizes
Greeting SignThe default three-line meet-and-greet sign, built from tags like passenger name and company
Accounts, Calendar, QuotesAccount numbers auto or manual · required account fields (the cause of "payment method is required" pop-ups) · calendar default view and week start
ReservationsPop-up vs in-page editing · autocomplete · auto-populate hours / passengers / stops / distance · read-back script · credit card required · vehicle-type vs car warning · copy and round-trip behaviour
Settle, Receivables, PayablesWhether unsettled trips can be invoiced · alert after N hours for done-but-unsettled trips · driver hours from trip duration or garage times
Driver AnywhereWhich app rate fields map to which line items · wait-time grace periods (airport vs non-airport) · when drivers must collect payment

6.2 System users: giving colleagues access

In plain words — Every person who logs in needs their own user. The company's administrator creates it; the person then gets an email to set a password. Sharing logins is not allowed — every change in the system is stamped with the user who made it.
1OpenMy Office›Company Settings›System Users › Add
2Fill inFirst and last name, mobile, email (the invite goes here), username (best practice: the same email), primary role (reporting only)
3SaveAn invite email is sent within a minute. It expires within a day — if it goes stale, use Forgot password on the login page.
4Restrict (optional)New users see everything by default. Untick modules or sub-modules they should not open.

By module

Block whole icons (My Office, Reports, Dispatch, Settle, Receivables, Payables) or parts — e.g. allow invoicing but not payments, or hide System Users so someone cannot re-enable their own access.

By schedule

A date range for temporary staff, or hours and weekdays (9–6, Mon–Fri) for shift workers.

By IP address

Allow or block specific office IP addresses so a login only works from the office.

Off-boarding

Edit the user: Activation → Inactive, Lock-out → Locked, note the reason. Never delete — history stays attached to the user.

Password rules

Back office: at least 12 characters with upper and lower case, a number and a symbol, and not containing the username. Driver Anywhere and passenger apps: at least 7 characters with the same mix. The Company ID is never emailed — the admin tells new users what it is.

6.3 Service types: what the company sells

In plain words — A service type is a product on the menu: "Airport pickup", "Hourly as directed", "Point to point", "Wedding charter". Picking one on a reservation decides how the price is worked out and which vehicles are offered. Set these up first; everything else refers to them.

Found under My Office›Company Settings›System Settings›Service Types. Each one has:

Code & name

A short code (AIRA) and an internal name (From Airport). Codes are arbitrary but permanent once used.

Custom label

What customers see on the website, e.g. "Airport departure — please book 2 hours ahead".

Pricing type

Fixed (zone to zone), Hourly, Per passenger, Distance (per mile) or Fixed-or-Distance (zone price first, per-mile if none). Pick one.

Rate matrix

Which rate sheet (Default, Summer…) this service type reads for fixed and distance prices.

Visible in ORES

Show it on the online booking widget or keep it back-office only.

Default mapping

One service type each must be marked as the company's point-to-point, airport arrival, airport departure and hourly. Quick Rate Lookup and the passenger app use this when a customer never chooses a service type.

Try the price resolver

Change the pricing type and whether a zone pair exists, and see what the customer gets.

Lesson 4 of 10

6.4 Vehicle types and the fleet

In plain words — A vehicle type is a category on the menu ("SUV", "Sedan", "Sprinter"). The fleet is the list of real cars with plate numbers. Prices are attached to the type, never to the individual car — three different SUVs under the "SUV" type all cost the customer the same.
Company Resources › Vehicle Types

Add a vehicle type

  1. Enter a unique code (SUV, SED) and a title.
  2. Choose hourly or per-passenger as its main rate style.
  3. Passenger and luggage capacity — this is what the website checks, not the car's.
  4. Colour code for the dispatch grid; description and photo for the website.
  5. Tick the service types this vehicle may be used for. Unticked = never offered for that service.
  6. Optionally hide it from online booking or mark it accessible. Save.

Never delete a vehicle type — set it Inactive, or reports and old trips break.

Company Resources › Fleet

Add a car

  1. Code (SUV-3), description, make, model, year, colour, plate.
  2. Pick its vehicle type — this is the link that makes pricing and the dispatch warning work.
  3. Capacity, status Active. Everything else (VIN, insurance, mileage) is optional.

Set up all vehicle types first, then the cars.

Drivers

Company Resources›Drivers: name, mobile and carrier (for texts), licence, then the web access username/password and the Driver Anywhere settings tab — nothing reaches the app until that first box is ticked. Pay schedules per vehicle type live here too.

Airports & airlines

All airports are pre-loaded but inactive. Show All, find yours, set Active — that puts it in the reservation dropdown. Same for airlines; private airlines (FBOs) need an address.

Points of interest

Stadiums, hotels, venues the company goes to often, with a category and address, so they can be picked from the POI tab.

6.5 Rates: how a price is built

In plain words — A price on a trip is a short list of lines: a base fare, a tip, tax, maybe a fuel fee, maybe a discount. The System Rate Manager defines those lines once for the company, and each line is told what kind of number it is and what it is calculated on. Get that right and the maths is automatic.

My Office›Rate Management has four pages: System Rate Manager (the lines), Fixed Rates & Zones (zone-to-zone prices), Special Promotion Setup (promo codes) and Miscellaneous Fees (rule-based extras). Hourly, per-passenger and distance prices are set on the vehicle type instead.

Rate type

Fixed

One dollar amount. Flat Rate, Tolls, Parking.

Rate type

Multiplier

Quantity × amount. Per Hour, Per Pass, Extra Stops, Child Seats.

Rate type

Percentage

% of a defined base. Gratuity, Tax, Surcharge.

Discount (base)Deducted from base before everything else calculatesCorporate 10%
MiscellaneousAdded; excluded from gratuity/taxAirport fee, late-night fee

6.6 Fixed rates and zones

In plain words — "From the airport to downtown in an SUV is $165." That is a fixed rate: a set price between two zones. A zone is either an area (a city, or a group of zip codes) or an airport. Build the zones first, then the prices between them.
1Open the matrixRate Management›Fixed Rates & Zone Setup › pick the rate sheet (Default is the one customers use).
2Define zones (…)Area zone: code (SDAL), description, city or cities, state, zip codes. Airport zone: the FAA code as the zone code (DFW, DAL), city/zip blank.
3Add a rateFrom zone → to zone, vehicle type, price; optional tolls, parking, taxes. Tick Create reverse rate for the return direction.
4Bulk uploadHundreds of zones? Fill in support's spreadsheet templates (zones first, then rates — vehicle type codes must already exist).

Zip codes carve up a city

"Dallas" with no zips is one giant zone. Add zips and it shrinks to those zips — so you can make "North Dallas" and "South Dallas" with different prices.

Multiple rate sheets

Default, Summer, Event weekend… one is flagged as default; a service type or a customer account can point at a different sheet.

Fixed always wins online

If a zone pair exists, web customers see the fixed price and never the per-mile one. Back-office staff can still choose either tab.

Lesson 7 of 10

6.7 Hourly, per-passenger and distance rates

In plain words — These three are "rate × something": rate × hours, rate × passengers, rate × miles. Because the "something" comes from the trip, these prices live on the vehicle type (Company Resources › Vehicle Types › edit › Rates tab) — six clicks deep, and the place people most often can't find.

Hourly

Standard rate per hour, a minimum number of hours, optional tiers (hours 1–2 at $150, 3+ at $120) and a peak-rate schedule (one time block per weekday). Choose which multiplier line the result lands in — normally Per Hour.

Minimums are a gate, not a rounding rule: book below the minimum online and the vehicle is simply not offered.

Per passenger

Same idea: rate per passenger, minimum passengers, tiers, and a target line such as Per Pass. If that line is disabled in the System Rate Manager it won't appear as a choice — enable it first.

Distance

Per mile or km, in tiers: first 1 mi $65 · next 19 mi $0 · remaining $1.50 gives a $65 minimum that covers 20 miles. Alternatively a flat "minimum mileage charge" per sheet. Result goes into one flat-rate line or a set of multiplier lines (Company Preferences › Reservations › Auto-populate distance total — which is also the on-switch for Google address lookup).

Rates are snapshots

A reservation copies the rate table the moment it is created. Changing a rate later affects new reservations only; press Apply Rate Table again on an old one if it should be re-priced.

Stored Rates — Multiplier Rate
Per Hour — (Base Rate)Per Pass — (Base Rate)Extra Stops — (Base Rate)Per km — (Base Rate)Per Unit — (Base Rate)

A multiplier rate is a quantity × an amount. The rate itself only says which quantity to use — the amount comes from the price list.

Every one of these is "how many × how much": hours, passengers, extra stops, kilometres.

This is the wiring. The preference is what turns a number you typed on the trip into a line on the price. Without it, the hours sit in the box and never reach the money.
Lesson 8 of 10

6.8 Promo codes, fees and extras

Rate Management › Special Promotion Setup

Promo codes

A code the customer types online or an agent picks on the reservation. Rules limit where it works: service types, zip codes, vehicle types, airports, a date or date range. Two flavours — Is Discount ticked = a % or $ off the base rates (flat, per hour, per passenger, or tiered); unticked = a replacement rate that overrides every line. Set old codes Inactive rather than deleting so reports keep working (Sales Revenue report › filter by promo code).

Rate Management › Miscellaneous Fees

Rule-based fees

"$20 late-night fee when pickup is in Dallas, point-to-point, between 1:00 and 6:59 AM." Pick the line item it posts to, Mandatory (auto-applies online) or Optional (the back office asks), then the criteria: service types, vehicle types, airport codes, pickup/drop-off text, dates and times.

Credit-card processing fee

Two ways. Everyone pays by card → a percentage line in Surcharge 4 in the System Rate Manager (e.g. 3%, primary). Only some do → make the line with default 0 and add a Mandatory misc fee that applies on the right service/vehicle types, so ORES and the app add it automatically.

Child seats & airport meet options

Child seat: a multiplier line (default $15 × 0); the reservation's child-seat count fills the quantity when auto-populate child seats is on. Meet options: Company Preferences › Reservations › Airport Meet Option — separate prices and labels for curbside and inside ("Meet & Greet"), shown online and in the back office.

Lesson 9 of 10

6.9 Reservation preferences that shape the screen

In plain words — These switches change what the reservation screen does while you type. When a trainee says "it didn't do that on my screen yesterday", it is one of these.
SettingEffect on the reservation screen
Use autocomplete (exclude non-account data)Whether typing in Billing Contact shows account matches at all.
Auto-populate distance total → one fixed rate / set of multipliersThe "on switch" for distance pricing and Google address lookup. Off = no verification, no mileage. Applies per service type.
Auto-populate number of hours into rate multiplierCopies trip duration into the Per Hour quantity, for the chosen service types.
Auto-populate number of passengers / stops / child seatsSame idea for Per Pass, Extra Stops and Child Seat multipliers.
Copy / Round-trip optionsWhat is carried over (rates, affiliate data, links) when duplicating.
Open reservations in pop-up vs. modalHow editing from Dispatch behaves.

Status workflow mapping

System Settings›System Mapping. The company's own status names mapped to Limo Anywhere's lifecycle, separately for operator, driver and affiliate flows; optional time stamping per status.

Email confirmation on first save

Messaging & Template Settings›General. Most companies turn this off and send confirmations on purpose via Email/Fax.

Online booking (ORES) rules

Company Settings›Online Reservations. Show prices or not, quote/book fallback, accepted payment methods, card required, auto-accept lead time, blackout hours, colours and the embed code for the website.

Lesson 10 of 10

6.10 Knowledge check

Knowledge check 06

Configuration

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

A trip's gratuity is calculating on top of the state tax. What is wrong?

Gratuity calculates on the total of the Base group; a "tax" placed in Base will be tipped on. The group, not the name, drives the math.

You lowered the SUV hourly rate from $150 to $120. A reservation created last week still shows $150. Why?

Rate changes only affect new reservations; existing ones keep their snapshot unless you re-apply the rate table.

Addresses save without any Google verification and no mileage is ever calculated. Which preference is off?

Despite its name, that setting is the switch for Google lookup and distance pricing.

To make a fixed rate from Dallas Love Field to downtown, the airport zone's code must be…

Airport zones match on the FAA code; area zones match on city/state/zip.
Wrap-up

What you should be able to do now

Explain

The billing / booking / passenger model, farm-in vs farm-out, and how fixed, hourly, distance and per-passenger pricing differ.

Navigate

Give any setting as a My Office path, know New Res vs Reservations, and use Rate, Find and right-click on Dispatch.

Book

Take a call to a saved, priced, dispatch-ready reservation — attaching the account properly, storing routing with the right action, applying a rate, and setting the status that actually notifies the driver.

Dispatch

Read the board, put a driver and car on a trip, offer or assign it, follow the driver's statuses and spot the exceptions.

Diagnose

Trace "why did it price like that?" back to service type → vehicle type → rate group → preference.

All six knowledge checks passed.

Next in the GroundOps programme: LA 301 (dispatch, Driver Anywhere, settling & invoicing) and LA 401 (payables, scheduled messaging, LA Net, reporting).
